source_title: Franchise Brands plc Annual Report and Accounts 2021
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 52, 59 and 60 state that the report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 2 March 2022; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 17% to £57.7m, adjusted EBITDA 28% to £8.5m and profit before tax 57% to £5.8m, while net cash increased to £6.5m. The Group reported strong recovery despite the first-quarter lockdown; isolated profitability weakness in one service line was outweighed by broad B2B and B2C growth.
already_announced_exclusion: The Barking Mad office closure, B2C consolidation, Azura integration and pandemic operating measures disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Broad revenue, adjusted profit, statutory profit and net-cash growth provide exceptionally strong contrary evidence against limited service-line pressure.

source_title: Franchise Brands plc Annual Report and Accounts 2023
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 81, 110, 111, 121 and 122 state that the report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 19 June 2024; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 74% and adjusted EBITDA 97% after the Pirtek acquisition, but statutory profit before tax fell 50% to £5.0m and acquisition funding moved the Group from £9.8m net cash to £74.7m net debt. Underlying businesses were cash-generative and performed strongly, although some customer sectors softened and used-oil pricing declined. Pirtek integration, central IT consolidation and debt-repayment priorities were already announced.
already_announced_exclusion: Pirtek integration, centralised international IT, the pause on further large acquisitions and the announced debt-repayment programme were public or underway before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Acquisition leverage and lower statutory profit create moderate pressure, but near-doubled adjusted earnings, resilient demand, strong cash generation and successful integration provide substantial offsets.
